title: Cities: Skylines | Power, Politics, & Planning: Episode 6: Public Housing Part 2
premise: donoteat01 argues that privatized housing subsidies, redevelopment incentives, demolition, and limits on collective labor investment obstruct housing as a public good. A fictional neighborhood’s dispersal leads through Boston and Philadelphia examples toward tenant organizing and universal public housing. These are attributed arguments, not an independent historical fact-check.
coverage: All 85 original contact sheets and one supplemental sheet were visually inspected: 1,013 original indexed frames plus appended canonical frame1014, totaling1,014 indexed frames spanning the full video, plus 10 native targeted stills at 120, 245.9, 1110, 1125, 1989, 2947, 3110, 3196.4, 3555, and 3805 seconds. Sampling is every five-second bin plus detected scene changes, not continuous playback; short unrepresented gags may remain. All selected frameNumber values refer to inspected index tiles. The shared renderer derives FULL speech from every transcript word exactly once using panel start boundaries; no manual dialogue excerpts or endSeconds remain. Machine ASR is not human-verified speech. Full narrative/evidence: story-sheets/7oeLnpAmmfI.md; speech: transcripts/7oeLnpAmmfI.json. The North Korean national anthem background cue in the approximately 07:44.3–09:30 panel region is annotated from an explicit user observation, with coarse timing and no performer or exact cue-boundary claim. Other empty sound arrays mean unannotated, not silence. No non-speech audio was invented from stills or ASR. A second visual pass resolved the inside-out cow, party-logo pairing, and a brief IRA pun; the latter is evidenced by a targeted native still and appended canonical frame1014 because its payoff fell between the original samples. Separate setup and payoff panels now illustrate both actual images.
